name: Lake Drachensee Ehrwald
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Drachensee at 1,910 m near Ehrwald: High-alpine mountain lake directly below the Coburger Hütte, famous for deep-emerald waters and dramatic limestone crags.
beschreibung:
Overview

The legendary Lake Drachensee lies in the Mieming Range above the village of Ehrwald (Reutte district) at a breathtaking elevation of 1,910 metres above sea level. Nestled directly beneath the historic Coburger Hütte (1,920 m) and framed by the sheer limestone walls of the Vorderer Tajakopf (2,450 m) and the Ehrwalder Sonnenspitze, it ranks as one of the highest and deepest natural alpine tarns in the region. Reaching maximum water depths exceeding 28 metres, the crystalline lake glistens in enchanting shades of deep emerald-green and cobalt-blue depending on the angle of sunlight.

Route & Requirements

The lake owes its name ("Dragon Lake") to ancient Tyrolean folklore, which tells of a ferocious dragon lurking in its depths guarding a sunken city. Today, it captivates mountain hikers, alpinists, and via ferrata enthusiasts. Fed by subterranean karst springs and lingering snowfields, the lake drains through underground fissures to nourish Lake Seebensee lying roughly 260 vertical metres below. Perched on a rock plateau directly above the water, the DAV Coburger Hütte (built in 1901) offers shelter, meals, and overnight lodging. From its sun terrace, visitors enjoy iconic panoramic views plunging down into Lake Drachensee and stretching across towards the Wetterstein mountain chain. For rock climbers, it serves as the base for the formidable Tajakante via ferrata and summit ascents of the Sonnenspitze.

Visit & Arrival

Lake Drachensee is accessible along marked mountain trails during the hut season from early June through early October. Access to the lake is free. The classic ascent begins at the upper station of the Ehrwalder Almbahn cable car (1,502 m): an easy trail leads in roughly 1.5 hours to Lake Seebensee (1,657 m), followed by a steep 45-minute switchback mountain path climbing 260 vertical metres up to the Coburger Hütte and the lakeshore (total hiking time approx. 2.5 hours; sturdy footwear and surefootedness required). Arriving by car: via the B179 to Ehrwald and follow signs to the Ehrwalder Almbahn base terminal. By public transit: take the train to Ehrwald station and transfer to the local hiker bus directly to the cable car.

Tips

Even on hot summer days, water temperatures hover around a brisk 8 to 10 °C. Enjoying freshly cooked Kaiserschmarrn pancakes on the Coburger Hütte terrace while admiring the lake is an essential experience. The ridge trail between Seebensee and Drachensee provides renowned vantage points overlooking both mountain gems simultaneously.
oeffnungszeiten: June to early October during alpine hut season freely accessible
